classification.difficultyReason: Choose a usable concentration scale and turn the supplied reciprocal logarithm into a sketch with the correct intercept, asymptote and direction.

content.prompt: Using $\mathrm{pH}=\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{1}{C}\right)$, draw a graph of pH against the hydronium ion concentration $C$ in $\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$.

answer.short: A decreasing logarithmic curve for $C>0$, crossing the horizontal axis at $(1,0)$ and approaching the vertical asymptote $C=0$.
answer.worked:
Put $C$ on the horizontal axis and pH on the vertical axis. Use a linear scale on each axis.

$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{pH}&=\log_{10}\!\left(\frac{1}{C}\right)\\\mathrm{pH}&=-\log_{10}C\end{align*}$$

Plot $(0.1,1)$, $(1,0)$ and $(2,-\log_{10}2)$. Draw a smooth decreasing curve through them. The curve rises without bound as $C$ approaches zero from the right and falls without bound as $C$ increases.

spec.description: Authored solution graph on linear axes. The source provides only the graphing instruction. The blue curve shows the model, with arrows showing its continuation.
spec.mathematics: pH = -log10(C), C > 0. The graph crosses at (1,0), decreases, and has vertical asymptote C = 0. The plotted parametrisation is (10^(-t),t).
